Bug_Title: Raw byte values should not be used in bitwise operations in combination with shifts
Bug_Details:
In Java, numeric promotions happen when two operands of an arithmetic expression have different sizes. More specifically, narrower operands get
promoted to the type of wider operands. For instance, an operation between a byte and an int , will trigger a promotion of
the byte operand, converting it into an int .
When this happens, the sequence of 8 bits that represents the byte will need to be extended to match the 32-bit long sequence that
represents the int operand. Since Java uses two’s complement notation for signed number types, the promotion will fill the missing
leading bits with zeros or ones, depending on the sign of the value. For instance, the byte 0b1000_0000 (equal to -128 in
decimal notation), when promoted to int , will become 0b1111_1111_1111_1111_1111_1111_1000_0000 .
When performing shifting or bitwise operations without considering that bytes are signed, the bits added during the promotion may have unexpected
effects on the final result of the operations.
Bug_Explanation: Raw byte values should not be used in bitwise operations in combination with shifts. In Java, numeric promotions happen when two operands of an arithmetic expression have different sizes. More specifically, narrower operands get promoted to the type of wider operands. When this happens, the sequence of 8 bits that represents the byte will need to be extended to match the 32-bit long sequence that represents the int operand. When performing shifting or bitwise operations without considering that bytes are signed, the bits added during the promotion may have unexpected effects on the final result of the operations.
Trigger_Explanation: The bug is triggered by the Java byte value 0b10000000 (or decimal -128) being bit-shifted right 24 positions. In this case, the most significant bit is copied into the new position, which will always be 1 for a negative number (-1), but for a positive number, the most significant bit is 0. Therefore, the result of the bitwise shift operation is always -1, regardless of the expected result.
